source.author: verg
source.text: Id metuens, veterisque memor Saturnia belli, prima quod ad Troiam pro caris gesserat Argis necdum etiam causae irarum saevique dolores exciderant animo: manet alta mente repostum iudicium Paridis spretaeque iniuria formae, et genus invisum, et rapti Ganymedis honores.
source.text_original: Id metuens, veterisque memor Saturnia belli, / prima quod ad Troiam pro caris gesserat Argis — / necdum etiam causae irarum saevique dolores / exciderant animo: manet alta mente repostum / iudicium Paridis spretaeque iniuria formae, / et genus invisum, et rapti Ganymedis honores.
source.text_english: Fearing this, and mindful of the old war, Saturnia, because of what she had first waged against Troy for her dear Argos, while the causes of her anger and the bitter pains had not yet even now fallen away from her heart: deep in her mind there remains stored the judgment of Paris and the insult of her slighted beauty, and the hated race, and the honors paid to stolen Ganymede.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: at Iuno Argolicas pariter Macetumque per urbes spargit inexpertos temptare parentibus austros Aesoniden; iam stare ratem remisque superbam poscere quos revehat rebusque in saecula tollat.
reuse.text_original: at Iuno Argolicas pariter Macetumque per urbes / spargit inexpertos temptare parentibus austros / Aesoniden; iam stare ratem remisque superbam / poscere quos revehat rebusque in saecula tollat.
reuse.text_english: But Juno, through the Argive cities and the cities of the Macedonians alike, spreads the word that Aeison’s son is to try winds untested by his father; already the ship stands and, proud of its oars, asks for those whom it may carry back and raise by its deeds to the ages.
